questions.stem: A student places a piece of iron into silver nitrate solution and observes silver crystals forming. She then places iron into magnesium sulfate solution and sees no change. What can she conclude about the reactivity order?

options.text: Silver > Iron > Magnesium
Iron > Silver > Magnesium
Magnesium > Iron > Silver
Magnesium > Silver > Iron

questions.explanation: Iron displaces silver from solution (so iron is more reactive than silver), but iron cannot displace magnesium (so magnesium is more reactive than iron). The correct order from most to least reactive is: Magnesium > Iron > Silver.

questions.stem: Potassium reacts vigorously with cold water, while iron only reacts with steam. Which explanation best accounts for this difference?

options.text: Potassium is a smaller atom so it reacts faster
Potassium loses its outer electron more easily than iron loses its outer electrons
Iron is a transition metal so it cannot react with water at all
Potassium has more electrons to lose than iron

questions.explanation: Potassium is higher in the reactivity series because it loses its single outer electron very easily - the electron is far from the nucleus and weakly held. Iron's outer electrons are harder to remove. More reactive metals lose electrons more readily. Iron can react with steam, just not cold water.

questions.stem: A jeweller needs to store hydrochloric acid in a metal container. Which metal from the reactivity series would be most suitable?

options.text: Zinc, because it is relatively cheap
Copper, because it is below hydrogen in the reactivity series
Magnesium, because it is strong
Iron, because it is commonly available

questions.explanation: Metals below hydrogen in the reactivity series (copper, silver, gold, platinum) do not react with dilute acids. Copper would not react with hydrochloric acid, making it suitable for storage. Zinc, magnesium, and iron are all above hydrogen and would react with the acid, producing hydrogen gas and dissolving.

questions.stem: Four metals W, X, Y, and Z are tested. W displaces X from solution. Z does not displace Y. X displaces Y from solution. Which is the correct order from most to least reactive?

options.text: W, X, Y, Z
Z, Y, X, W
W, X, Z, Y
W, Z, X, Y

questions.explanation: W displaces X, so W > X. X displaces Y, so X > Y. Z does not displace Y, so Y > Z (or Z is less reactive than Y). Combining: W > X > Y > Z. The order from most to least reactive is W, X, Y, Z.

questions.stem: Gold is found naturally as the pure metal in riverbeds, while aluminium is only found combined in ores like bauxite. What does this tell us about these metals?

options.text: Gold is more reactive, so it resists combining with other elements
Aluminium is very unreactive, which is why it stays in ore form
Gold is very unreactive, so it does not combine with other elements in nature
This is just due to how common each element is in the Earth's crust

questions.explanation: Very unreactive metals like gold are found native (as pure elements) because they do not readily react with oxygen, water, or other substances in the environment. Aluminium is very reactive and readily combines with oxygen, so it is always found as compounds in ores and must be extracted by electrolysis.
